source.author: verg
source.text: At saeva e speculis tempus dea nacta nocendi ardua tecta petit stabuli et de culmine summo pastorale canit signum cornuque recurvo Tartaream intendit vocem, qua protinus omne contremuit nemus et silvae insonuere profundae; audiit et Triviae longe lacus, audiit amnis sulfurea Nar albus aqua fontesque Velini, et trepidae matres pressere ad pectora natos.
source.text_original: At saeva e speculis tempus dea nacta nocendi / ardua tecta petit stabuli et de culmine summo / pastorale canit signum cornuque recurvo / Tartaream intendit vocem, qua protinus omne / contremuit nemus et silvae insonuere profundae; / audiit et Triviae longe lacus, audiit amnis / sulfurea Nar albus aqua fontesque Velini, / et trepidae matres pressere ad pectora natos.
source.text_english: But the savage goddess, having found from her watchtowers the time for harm, seeks the lofty roofs of the stall and from the highest ridge sounds the shepherd’s signal with a curved horn and sends forth a Tartarean voice, at which straightway every grove trembled and the deep woods rang out; Trivia’s lake heard it far off, and the Nar heard it, white with sulphurous water, and the springs of Velinus, and the frightened mothers pressed their children to their breasts.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: si fata reducunt te mihi, si trepidis placabile matribus aequor, possum equidem lucemque pati longumque timorem.
reuse.text_original: si fata reducunt / te mihi, si trepidis placabile matribus aequor, / possum equidem lucemque pati longumque timorem.
reuse.text_english: if the fates bring you back to me, if the sea can be calmed for trembling mothers, I can indeed endure both the daylight and the long fear.
